Using eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\ge 0\), Weyl integration gives
\[
I_n=\frac{\pi^2}{3}\int_{\lambda_i\ge 0}
e^{-n(e_2(\lambda)^2+(\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3)^8)}
\prod_{i<j}|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|\,d\lambda .
\]
The constant \(\pi^2/3\) follows by comparing both sides on the Gaussian
\(e^{-\operatorname{tr}(A^2)/2}\).

Put \(s=\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3\), \(p_i=\lambda_i/s\). On the simplex \(p_i\ge0,\sum p_i=1\), write
\[
q=p_1p_2+p_1p_3+p_2p_3.
\]
Since \(e_2=s^2q\), \(\prod|\lambda_i-\lambda_j|=s^3\prod|p_i-p_j|\), and \(d\lambda=s^2\,ds\,dp\),
\[
I_n=\frac{\pi^2}{12}n^{-3/2}\int_{\Delta}
\prod_{i<j}|p_i-p_j|
\int_0^\infty t^{1/2}e^{-q^2t-t^2/n}\,dt\,dp .
\]

Now pass from \(p\) to \(q,r=p_1p_2p_3\). The Jacobian is \(\prod|p_i-p_j|\). For fixed \(q\), the allowed \(r\)-length is
\[
L(q)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{9q-2+2(1-3q)^{3/2}}{27},&0\le q\le \frac14,\\[1ex]
\dfrac{4(1-3q)^{3/2}}{27},&\frac14\le q\le \frac13.
\end{cases}
\]
The full simplex contributes a factor \(6\), so define \(h(q)=6L(q)\). Near \(q=0\),
\[
h(q)=\frac32q^2+O(q^3),
\]
which is the source of the logarithm.

Let
\[
F_n(q)=\int_0^\infty t^{1/2}e^{-q^2t-t^2/n}\,dt.
\]
Then
\[
\int_0^{1/3}h(q)F_n(q)\,dq
=\frac{3\sqrt\pi}{16}\log n
+\sqrt\pi\left(\frac{3\gamma}{16}+\frac94\log2-\frac{21}{8}\right)+o(1).
\]
The finite part comes from subtracting \(\frac32q^2\); explicitly,
\[
\int_0^{1/3}\frac{h(q)-\frac32q^2}{q^3}\,dq
=3\log2+\frac32\log3-\frac{15}{4},
\]
and the \(\log3\) terms cancel with the endpoint contribution from \(q=1/3\).

Therefore
\[
I_n=
\frac{\pi^{5/2}}{64}n^{-3/2}\log n
+\frac{\pi^{5/2}}{64}n^{-3/2}
\left(\gamma+12\log2-14\right)+o(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{\gamma+12\log 2-14}.
\]
